summary: The root جحم (jHm) relates to intense heat and burning. It describes live coals, a fiercely hot place, and metaphorically, the intense part or vehemence of battle.
lane: جَاحِمٌ جاحم : see جَحِيمٌ . Also Live coals ( جَمْرٌ ) vehemently burning or blazing or flaming. (K.) And a place vehemently hot; (S, K;) as also . (K.) El-Aashà says, المَوْتُ جَاحِمٌ [app. meaning (assumed tropical:) Death is like a burning, or fiercelyburning, fire ]. (S.) See also جَحْمَةٌ . -b2- جَاحِمُ الجَرْبِ The main part [or the thick ] of the war or battle: (K:) or the straitness thereof: (TA:) and the vehemence of the fight or slaughter, in the scene thereof. (K.) You say, اِصْطَلَى بِجَاحِمِ الحَرْبِ (tropical:) [ He warmed himself with the heat, or vehemence, of the battle ]. (TA.) -b3- الجَاحِمَةُ Fire: (TA:) or, [as an epithet,] fire burning, burning brightly or fiercely, blazing, or flaming. (Ham p. 77.)
